About the Company & Role Our client is a creative media production company specialising in producing professional visual content for businesses within the property, building, and construction sectors. The company provides a range of creative services, including photography, videography, aerial footage, and digital content production, helping businesses showcase their properties, projects, and services through compelling visual presentations. They are looking for a talented and detail-oriented Video Editor who can transform raw footage into polished, cinematic, and engaging video content that captures the quality and appeal of each project. The role involves editing various types of footage, including property walkthroughs, architectural spaces, construction developments, and commercial project showcases, while maintaining a consistent and professional visual style. The successful candidate will be expected to produce approximately 2–3 completed videos daily, balancing creative execution, technical quality, and production efficiency. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced editor who enjoys visual storytelling, understands cinematic editing techniques, and can deliver high-quality content in a fast-paced creative environment.

Key Responsibilities Video Editing & Post-Production

• Edit raw video footage into professional, engaging, and cinematic video productions.

• Produce approximately 2–3 completed videos per day while maintaining consistent quality and creative standards.

• Create property walkthroughs, real estate promotional videos, architectural showcases, and construction project features.

• Apply professional editing techniques, including sequencing, transitions, pacing, music integration, and visual storytelling.

• Perform colour correction and colour grading to achieve a polished and consistent cinematic look.

• Edit and incorporate drone footage, interior and exterior shots, and other visual assets into cohesive video presentations.

• Adapt editing styles based on project requirements, target audiences, and creative direction.

AI-Assisted Editing & Content Production

• Utilise AI-powered video editing and enhancement tools, particularly Higgsfield, to improve production workflows and creative output.

• Apply AI-assisted effects, enhancements, and visual elements while ensuring the authenticity and quality of the final content.

• Produce videos in different formats and aspect ratios, including landscape and vertical formats for various digital platforms.

• Optimise video content for online marketing and social media distribution.

• Ensure proper audio synchronisation, sound quality, captions, and overall video presentation.

Quality Control & Project Management

• Review all completed videos to ensure accuracy, consistency, and professional production standards before delivery.

• Manage multiple editing assignments and consistently meet daily production targets and deadlines.

• Maintain organised project files, raw footage, editing assets, and completed outputs.

• Implement feedback and revision requests promptly while maintaining attention to detail.

• Identify opportunities to improve editing workflows, turnaround times, and production efficiency.

Creative Collaboration & Brand Consistency

• Maintain consistency with the company's established creative direction and visual standards.

• Contribute creative ideas and recommendations to enhance the quality and impact of video content.

• Adjust editing approaches based on project requirements and client expectations.

• Collaborate with the team to ensure timely delivery and alignment with production objectives.

Qualifications & Requirements Essential Requirements

• At least 3 years of professional experience in video editing or post-production.

• Advanced proficiency in Final Cut Pro.

• Must have access to a Mac computer capable of running Final Cut Pro.

• Strong understanding of cinematic editing, storytelling, transitions, and video composition.

• Demonstrated experience in colour correction and professional colour grading.

• Proficiency in AI-powered video production tools, particularly Higgsfield.

• Strong understanding of audio synchronisation, sound design, music integration, and visual aesthetics.

• Ability to consistently deliver 2–3 completed videos per day without compromising quality.

• Excellent attention to detail and ability to work independently in a deadline-driven environment.

Preferred Qualifications

• Previous experience editing real estate, property marketing, architectural, or construction-related videos.

• Experience incorporating drone footage into professional video productions.

• Knowledge of motion graphics, captions, sound design, and visual effects.

• Familiarity with other AI-assisted video editing and content creation tools.

• Experience working with real estate professionals, property developers, builders, contractors, or commercial clients.

• Higgsfield: AI-assisted video production, enhancement, and creative effects.

• Audio Editing Tools: Sound design, audio synchronisation, and music integration.

Skills & Competencies
• Creative Storytelling: Ability to transform raw footage into visually compelling narratives.

• Time Management: Capable of handling multiple projects and meeting daily production targets.

• Adaptability: Can work across different video styles and project requirements.

About AudienceView
AudienceView is passionate about helping live event organizations bring people together through unforgettable experiences. Our unified event commerce platform helps organizations better understand, engage, and grow their audiences while creating stronger relationships and more connected experiences across the entire event journey.
We support organizations across performing arts, music, athletics, higher education, fairs, festivals, attractions, and more. By combining technology, audience intelligence, and deep industry expertise, AudienceView helps organizations make informed decisions, simplify operations, and build sustainable growth.

Four core values set the tempo for how we work:

• We are people first.

• We are innovative.

• We are results-driven.

• We are transparent.

AudienceView is made up of people who believe wholeheartedly in the power and magic of live events. Come transform live entertainment with us.

Why we'd want to work with you
We are looking for a Digital Marketing Manager to own and scale our B2B demand generation engine. In this role, you will drive pipeline growth and lower customer acquisition costs (CAC) by orchestrating high-impact paid campaigns, targeted ABM programs, and sophisticated marketing automation workflows. If you are a data-driven marketer who loves connecting the dots between paid media, email nurtures, and sales execution, we want to talk to you.

What you'll do:

• Paid Search & Paid Ads: Own Google Ads and LinkedIn campaigns end-to-end—including strategy, budgeting, bidding, keyword research, audience building, and creative testing—to drive pipeline and optimize CAC. Expand into review platforms (G2, Capterra) where it makes strategic sense.

• Email Marketing & Nurture: Design and execute email programs in Pardot, focusing on precise segmentation, multi-touch nurture tracks, trigger-based sends, and lifecycle campaigns tailored to key buyer personas.

• Account-Based Marketing (ABM): Own the tooling, account scoring, and 1-to-many ABM framework. Partner with Sales and Revenue Operations to build tiered target account lists and deliver personalized, programmatic campaigns.

• Marketing Automation & CRO: Build, maintain, and troubleshoot workflows, lead scoring models, and routing rules to ensure leads reach Sales quickly and accurately. Improve website conversion rates through landing pages, form optimization, and CRO experiments.

• Reporting & Attribution: Track performance across paid, email, ABM, and automation. Report on spend, conversion rates, pipeline velocity, and CAC by channel to guide data-driven budget allocation.

• Test & Optimize: Continually run experiments across channels, messaging, and funnel paths to scale what works and cut what doesn't.

• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with Sales, BDRs, RevOps, and Product Marketing to ensure airtight alignment on targeting, messaging, and lead handoffs.

What you'll need:

• 4+ years of B2B digital demand generation experience , with a proven track record of scaling inbound pipeline.

• Paid Media Expertise: Hands-on experience managing and optimizing Google Ads and LinkedIn Ads with a focus on efficiency (CAC) and revenue generation.

• Marketing Automation: Strong command of Pardot (or similar enterprise automation tools), email compliance, segmentation, and lead-scoring frameworks.

• Technical Stack: Proficiency with Salesforce, Google Analytics / GA4, and WordPress (or equivalent CMS).

• Analytical Mindset: Exceptional problem-solving skills with a deep understanding of marketing attribution models and funnel metrics.

• Project Management: Strong cross-functional collaboration skills across Marketing and Sales teams.

• Mindset: A curious, self-starting operator who thrives in a fast-paced environment and loves continuous learning.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

• High-Intent MQLs: Volume and lead quality by channel and segment.

• Marketing-Generated Pipeline: Total opportunity value created.

• Pipeline Velocity & Conversion Rates: Website, funnel, nurture, and trial-to-paid conversion performance.

• Engagement & Progression: Email engagement metrics and target account movement through the ABM funnel.

Few people tick every box on a list like this. If most of it sounds like you and the rest sounds like something you'd love to learn, we still want to hear from you.

Why work at AudienceView

• Our work helps bring live experiences to life. From Broadway tours and symphony performances to music festivals, museums, universities, attractions, and community events, our software helps organizations of all sizes connect people with unforgettable experiences every day.

• We're fans, not just vendors. Our teams include former box office staff, front-of-house crew, local musicians, season ticket holders, arts advocates, and lifelong eventgoers. That shared passion for live experiences is at the heart of everything we do.

• You'll solve meaningful challenges at scale. Supporting over 2800 organizations and millions of ticket buyers means working on complex, rewarding problems. Whether it's powering major on-sales, improving the patron experience, or helping clients grow their audiences, you'll see the impact of your work firsthand.

• We're remote-first with a live-events heart. Work alongside globally based colleagues who share a genuine passion for the arts, culture, sports, entertainment, and live experiences that bring people together.

• Diversity and inclusion are paramount to building our culture. The data is abundantly clear that diverse teams are more successful because they offer different perspectives, increased innovation, faster problem-solving and higher employee engagement among other benefits.

How we hire — our run of show
No black holes and no endless rounds. Here's the run of show, so you know exactly what's coming and when:

• Screening & Resume Review: Our Talent Acquisition team will evaluate all resumes and select candidates for a video screening call for 30 minutes.

• Hiring Manager Interview (30 minutes): Meet with the hiring manager to speak in detail about your relevant experience and learn more about the role.

• Meet More of the Team (60 minutes): Meet more team members to learn more about the work culture and expectations.

• Case Study Interview (45 minutes): Meet with the hiring manager again to complete a quick case study.

Every interview is held face to face over Microsoft Teams with a member of our team on camera. If we interview you, we will tell you whether a hiring decision has been made for this role within 45 days of your last interview.

How we use artificial intelligence in hiring
We use AI in one place only. Our hiring team may use Microsoft Copilot to transcribe interviews and draft interview notes, so that interviewers can concentrate on the conversation instead of typing. You will always know before any recording or AI note-taking begins, and you can ask us to take notes manually instead — it will not affect your application.
We do not use AI to screen, assess, rank or select applicants, and no automated system makes a hiring decision at any stage. Every shortlisting, interview and offer decision is made by people on our hiring team.

Equal opportunity, inclusion and accessibility
Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at AudienceView. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our clients, the communities where we operate, and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified people of every background.
We are committed to an accessible hiring process and provide accommodations and adjustments to applicants with disabilities on request, at every stage of recruitment and employment.

How to spot a genuine AudienceView offer
AudienceView does not offer employment to anyone without first ensuring that qualified candidates speak directly with a member of the hiring team. All qualifying conversations take place face to face over Microsoft Teams. We do not make offers of employment without meeting candidates, we never make an offer by text message, and we never ask candidates to pay a fee. If you are asked for personal or financial information by text, or before you have met a member of our hiring team, please disregard it.

Ready to join the show?
If this role sounds like your kind of show and your experience lines up with what we’re looking for, we’d love to hear from you. We’re grateful for every application we receive; however, only qualified candidates selected to move forward in our hiring process will be contacted.

In 1977, Charles and Ray Eames began a film with a picnic beside Chicago’s lakefront. Over the next nine minutes, Powers of Ten traveled out toward distant galaxies and back into the microscopic world inside a human hand. An enormous subject became a journey you could follow, built around a simple change in perspective. Images, language, movement, and sound brought the idea to life together.

That’s the kind of creative thinking we’re looking for at Mercury: finding a compelling idea inside something complex, then bringing together the people and crafts that make it unforgettable.

We’re looking for a Creative Director to build and lead Brand Narrative , a new team within Brand Creative. You’ll turn company strategy, product truths, customer insight, and cultural observations into original concepts for our most important launches, campaigns, and brand moments. You’ll originate ideas yourself and stay closely involved as they become finished work.

Your background might be in art direction, design, or copywriting. What matters is your ability to develop exceptional concepts, recognize the best idea wherever it comes from, and bring the whole creative studio together to make it real. Whatever your starting discipline, you’ll bring deep experience in film-led storytelling.

You’ll lead Brand Narrative in close creative partnership with your peers leading Brand Design and Writing. Together, you’ll shape concepts, language, and visual expression from the beginning, bringing distinct perspectives and shared ownership to the work. You’ll contribute strong ideas of your own, invite others to challenge and improve them, and build on theirs. This is a role for someone who enjoys making work together, not developing ideas in isolation and handing them off.

You’ll also shape what Brand Narrative becomes. That means building its culture, developing its people, and establishing ways of working that make the entire studio more creatively ambitious. The opportunity is to make great work while building a team that can keep making it.

What you’ll do

In your first year, your focus will be roughly 70% leading creative development for our highest-priority launches and campaigns, and 30% building the Brand Narrative function.

• Originate and lead big creative ideas. Partner with Product Marketing and Brand Marketing on the brief, then turn the agreed audience, opportunity, and product proof into original creative concepts. Develop ideas that can take distinctive forms across film, social, out-of-home, digital, experiences, and partnerships.

• Bring ambitious concepts to life with your creative peers and the full studio. Work side by side with the Brand Design and Writing leads and their teams from the earliest explorations through delivery. Develop ideas together, exchange thoughtful critique, and make creative choices that draw on each discipline’s expertise. Stay hands-on, contribute through your own craft, and partner closely with Motion and Production throughout. For film, remain closely involved through scripts, visual development, production, and the final edit.

• Build audience and distribution thinking into the idea. Shape concepts around how people will discover, watch, and share the work. Work with marketing partners to consider channels and viewing contexts from the beginning, so the work belongs where people encounter it rather than simply being resized to fit.

• Push beyond the first good answer, and learn quickly. Lead thoughtful concept development and critique. Use rough scripts, prototypes, and AI tools to test ideas quickly, learn, and move the strongest work forward. Know when to keep exploring and when to commit, then protect what makes an idea interesting through feedback and production.

• Find opportunities before a brief arrives. Bring curiosity about Mercury’s products, customers, and the wider world. Develop proactive ideas and cultural opportunities that give the brand something meaningful to say or do.

• Help decide where creative ambition matters most. Partner early with Product Marketing, Brand Marketing, Product Design, Comms, and Insights. Help identify which moments deserve our largest creative investment, present recommendations to senior leadership, and use results from marketing and insights partners to inform what comes next.

• Build and lead Brand Narrative. Define the team’s purpose, priorities, creative standards, and ways of working. Help hire and develop the team, shaping its structure and capabilities. Set clear expectations, and coach people to grow their judgment and conceptual strength.

• Create a culture where the best idea wins. Make room for experimentation, honest feedback, and contributions across disciplines. Lead with generosity and conviction, share ownership of the work, and help people challenge one another without making creativity a competition for credit.

• Build practices that strengthen the work. Establish a clear path from insight and an agreed brief to concept and execution, with useful critique and close collaboration throughout. Develop relationships with external creatives and agencies who can add a distinctive perspective or capability when needed.

What you’ll bring

• A strong creative foundation in art direction, design, or copywriting. Your portfolio shows original concepts developed into ambitious, well-crafted work across multiple formats. You can explain what you contributed, how the idea evolved, and how collaboration made it better.

• Deep film experience. You’ve developed film-led ideas from concept through production, with strong instincts for story, scripts, performance, pacing, and sound. You understand how these choices work together to make an audience feel something, not just make a film look good.

• A track record of deep creative collaboration with design and writing peers. You’ve led ambitious multidisciplinary work from concept through production by building trusted partnerships. You bring a clear point of view, listen closely, work through creative disagreements constructively, and recognize when someone else’s approach makes the work stronger. You can show how your collaborators shaped the outcome, not just what you personally originated.

• Strong taste, cultural awareness, and product curiosity. You can get close to a complex business or product, find the human truth within it, and turn that understanding into something clear, surprising, and memorable.

• Experience developing creative people and shaping how a team works. You give specific, useful feedback, set a high bar with care, and create an environment where people can take creative risks. You’re excited to build a new function, including the everyday practices that give it a culture.

• Clear communication and sound judgment. You can rally people around an ambitious concept, explain why it deserves investment, and navigate competing perspectives without losing the idea. You take ownership in ambiguous situations and balance creative ambition with the need to move work forward.

What success looks like

A year in, you’ll have led major launches and film-led campaigns from original concept through finished work, with Brand Design and Writing as creative partners from the beginning. The studio’s disciplines will have shaped the work together, with audience and distribution informing the creative approach.

Brand Narrative will have a clear identity, shared creative standards, and working practices that help people test and develop stronger ideas together. Alongside planned launches, you’ll have established a pipeline of proactive opportunities that gives Mercury more ways to express its product ambition with originality and cultural relevance.

Please include a portfolio featuring film-led work and broader campaign concepts. We’d love to understand your role in developing the ideas, the choices you made through production, and how you brought the work to life with others.
